facts.text: The serial client sends a command plus its line terminator as ASCII and returns the stripped reply line
The RS-232 module command DS IG returns the ion-gauge pressure; the documented reply example is 1.20E-07
The upstream GP350 parser accepts a pressure reply written X.XXE+XX and returns the value in Torr
9.90E+09 is not a real pressure: the controller uses it when there is no valid reading, for example when the ion gauge is off
DGS returns the degas status as 1 or 0
DG ON and DG OFF control degas and answer OK or INVALID
At high pressure DG ON can answer OK while DGS still reports degas off
IG1 ON/OFF controls filament 1 and IG2 ON/OFF controls filament 2
IGB returns a two-digit filament status; the documented values are 00, 01, 10 and 11
The upstream simulator encodes IGB as 01 when filament 1 is on, 10 when filament 2 is on and 11 when both are on
The upstream simulator answers INVALID when a filament or degas switch already has the requested state
